scenario.prompt_to_agent:
After a maintenance event on router16, all Campus 1 PCs
(PC5-14) report intermittent reachability to Campus 2 and the
backbone. The mswitch0 SVI gateways still respond, but anything
beyond router16 is unreachable. Diagnose.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router16 ospfd
Mechanism: router16 is the L3 edge between mswitch0 (Campus 1
  multilayer switch) and the backbone (router7/router8/etc.).
  With router16's ospfd dead, mswitch0 loses its OSPF
  neighbor for the backbone direction; Campus 1's only
  uplink stops advertising and learning. Inside Campus 1
  routing continues (mswitch0 ↔ access switches) but no
  off-campus traffic.
Localization: router16
Root cause: ospfd not running on router16
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration on router16 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ospfd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router ospf` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ospfd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the ospf configuration is missing/empty on router16" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on router16

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ospfd back CONFIG-LESS and the ospf service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ospfd AND re-apply the `router ospf` configuration (network statements) on router16. A proposal that restores the missing ospf configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The maintenance event on router16 wiped its FRR configuration file
(/etc/frr/frr.conf) down to an empty skeleton. As a result, ospfd was
never launched by watchfrr (only zebra, mgmtd, and staticd are running
on router16). Without ospfd, router16 has only two connected routes in
its kernel RIB — 10.2.2.0/24 (bond0 toward mswitch0) and
172.30.1.0/24 (eth2 toward router7) — and no routes to any backbone
or Campus 2 prefix.

On the upstream side, router7 has a full OSPF topology except that it
has no route to 10.2.2.0/24 or the Campus 1 VLAN subnets
(172.16.10/24, 172.16.20/24, 172.16.30/24), because router16 never
re-established its OSPF adjacency on eth2 after maintenance.

On the downstream side, mswitch0 runs its own ospfd, which had
previously learned all backbone routes via router16. That adjacency
has now dropped (mswitch0's OSPF neighbor table is empty), but stale
"proto ospf" kernel routes pointing to 10.2.2.1 remain installed.
Consequently, Campus 1 PCs reach their mswitch0 SVI gateways
correctly, but all off-campus traffic is forwarded to router16 and
black-holed there, since router16 has no onward path. The intermittent
symptom is caused by these stale routes on mswitch0 still being
present but gradually expiring.

Root cause: The frr.conf on router16 was blanked during maintenance,
eliminating the OSPF process configuration and preventing ospfd from
starting.

Corrective fix: Restore the OSPF configuration in /etc/frr/frr.conf
on router16 — re-add the `router ospf` process block with appropriate
`network` or `interface` statements covering bond0 (10.2.2.0/24) and
eth2 (172.30.1.0/24), matching the area assignments used by router7
and mswitch0, then run `service frr restart` on router16.

per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly identifies router16 as the affected device and describes its ospfd/FRR configuration failure.
The agent explicitly identifies ospfd/OSPF as the failed component (ospfd not launched and OSPF configuration removed).

The agent recommends re-adding the missing `router ospf` configuration (network/interface statements for bond0 and eth2) and restarting the FRR service, which restores OSPF and matches the expected remediation.

The agent's investigation log contains direct command outputs that substantiate the core claims (ospfd absent, frr.conf empty, only connected routes on router16, mswitch0 still had ospfd and stale OSPF routes), and the writeup draws logical inferences from those observations. Minor extrapolation about timing/maintenance cause is acceptable given the evidence.
